summary: Community single-host deployment composes TORGNEXA application roles, canonical migrations, Keycloak and S3-compatible storage with generated credentials, loopback-only exposure and fail-closed startup ordering.

impacts.evidence: Deployment wiring does not create tenant shortcuts; application tenancy and RLS remain unchanged.
No default credentials are committed; local credentials are generated into mode-0600 .env and production remains externally secret-managed.
No public HTTP operation is added or changed; the deployment exposes the existing secure API composition only on loopback.
No event schema changes; Kafka listener topology only separates container-internal and localhost clients.
Connector SDK and provider admission are unchanged; connectors receive infrastructure through existing host configuration.
No schema migration is added; a one-shot runner applies the reviewed 54-file catalog and verifies SHA-256/history before application startup.
Non-root/read-only application images, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, generated secrets and loopback-only ports are enforced.
Deployment does not bypass approval or regulated-write policy; existing application policy remains authoritative.
No audit/lineage data model changes; migration/startup failures are explicit process failures rather than silent state changes.
Migration execution is checksum-aware/idempotent for applied catalog entries and fails on unknown/partial bootstrap state.
Backend network retains required outbound connectivity for provider/webhook egress while no data service is publicly exposed.
Healthchecks and dependency ordering provide local readiness evidence; production SLO qualification remains Task-066 deployment evidence.
Named persistent volumes and separate one-shot migration jobs make stop/restart explicit; destructive volume removal is not part of normal rollback.
Community deployment policy, shell syntax, canonical catalog parity and full repository gates are required.
